support_spans: intermittent compression-like chest pain
T-waves became upright in V2 to V4 during chest pain
inverted T-waves in leads V2 to V4 without chest pain
contradict_spans: Total occlusion at the ostium of the left anterior descending coronary artery

candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may be overlooked due to the focus on more common causes of chest pain like myocardial infarction, and the specific ECG changes during and without pain are key to its identification.

candidates.name: Wellens' Syndrome
support_spans: deeply inverted T-waves in leads V2 to V4
Total occlusion at the ostium of the left anterior descending coronary artery
contradict_spans: chest pain lasting several minutes each time, occurring during activities and relieved by rest
candidates.why: The deeply inverted T-waves in leads V2 to V4 are highly suggestive of Wellens' syndrome, a condition that often precedes a myocardial infarction due to a critical stenosis in the left anterior descending coronary artery.
candidates.protected_reason: This condition is less common and can be missed if the characteristic ECG findings are not recognized promptly, leading to a delay in necessary intervention.
